title: Contact Geometry for Generative Models: An Unbalanced Optimal Transport Formulation
claim: Standard transport maps leak mass between modes and bias toward high-growth regions; our unbalanced formulation adapts weights and step sizes to data structure.
layout: 3 panels, left-to-right: path diagram, trajectory comparison, face image strips; shared color gradient
description: Three adjacent panels share a vertical time axis (t from 0 to 1) and a spatial axis x. A pastel gradient background encodes the growth rate z^t, with a color bar on the far left running from + (orange) to − (blue). The left panel shows two bimodal marginal densities joined by noisy gray diffusion paths, purple OT lines and black UOT lines. Some purple lines cross between modes, while the black lines stay within their own mode. The middle panel compares WFR (brown squares) and CuOT (gold squares) trajectories from two start points x_a^0 and x_b^0. The WFR paths drift toward the other mode, and the CuOT paths stay nearly flat with adaptive step spacing. The right panel shows four rows of face-image interpolations with gold or brown borders. Rows are labeled with the same x notation, and the CuOT rows keep identity more consistently than the WFR rows.
caption: {Left: Two marginals connected by a diffusion process (noisy gray path), an OT map (\purpleline), and a \ac{UOT} map (\blackline), the latter preventing mode leakage by adapting sample weights according to the growth rate $z^t$. Middle-Right: Comparison between \ac{UOT} methods, namely \ac{WFR} (brown squares) and \ac{CUOT} (gold squares), in a dataset pairing experiment (App. [ref]). Our \ac{CUOT} method avoids bias toward high-growth regions and adapts the step size to the data structure.\looseness-1}
abstract: Real-world generative problems in biology, medical imaging, or robotics, rarely come with perfectly paired source and target distributions. While unbalanced Optimal Transport (uOT) provides a robust framework to bridge unpaired datasets via minimum-length paths in probability space, existing formulations based on the Wasserstein-Fisher-Rao (WFR) geometry introduce a structural bias toward high density regions, often triggering mode collapse. We introduce Contact unbalanced Optimal Transport (CuOT), a novel uOT formulation grounded in contact geometry that decouples density transport direction from mass growth to eliminate structural bias. This allows CuOT to adapt sampling steps to the local data structure, naturally reducing step sizes in high-density regions to prevent overshooting and ensuring stable convergence. The result is a stable, scalable path-length minimization solver that consistently outperforms WFR-based methods on biological dynamics reconstruction, unpaired image-to-image translation, and video generation.
